title: United’s retention of harassing pilot may have been criminally negligent, judge finds
summary: The airline allegedly learned of a police investigation into a pilot’s distribution of a worker’s intimate images in April 2024 but didn’t act until his arrest later that year.

title: Feds to propose H-1B fee that would stack with controversial $100K payment
summary: Employers should expect litigation against the new fee once it is finalized, a source told HR Dive, similar to what occurred after last year’s fee was announced by President Donald Trump.

title: EFAA covers claims that emerge during an arbitration proceeding, 9th Circuit says
summary: The parties in the case conducted arbitration proceedings for a full year — but that fact alone can’t prevent plaintiffs from seeking arbitration exemption, the court held.

title: Companies that roll back DEI don’t perform better financially, study says
summary: “Large corporations appear to have folded under pressure for no financial gain,” a public policy scholar wrote.

title: Week in review: Bank of America bans consecutive remote days
summary: We’re rounding up last week’s stories, including HR Dive’s summer reading list for 2026.

title: Beyond flexibility: Why partnership is becoming the new standard in HR services
summary: Today's employers expect more from their HR partner. See why trust, accountability and co-employment are redefining the HR services landscape.

title: Amazon worker fired shortly after disclosing pregnancy has discrimination claim, court rules
summary: The alleged close connection between her disclosure, restrictions on her overtime and her termination indicated adverse action based on the pregnancy, the court said.

title: Feds axe contractor affirmative action requirements in trio of final rules
summary: The documents follow up on one of President Donald Trump’s first orders that sought to alter the federal government’s antidiscrimination enforcement work.

title: Skilled labor demand is exploding. AI may be both a cause and a solution
summary: A survey by the National Fire Protection Association found that while AI is putting pressure on an already stretched fire and safety workforce, it is also making their jobs easier.

title: Women are significantly underrepresented in the AI workforce
summary: The gender disparity is even more pronounced in the highest-paying jobs and top executive levels, according to research from LinkedIn.
